title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X/S is a smooth relative curve, ω = Ω^1_{X/S} is invertible, and 2 is assumed invertible (left margin, with a later marginal query whether this is really needed). The page continues the previous one, where an extension L of O_X by ω was identified with P^1_{X/S}(ω)⊗ω^{-1}, the twisted bundle of first-order principal parts, up to factors -2 and -1/2.

Grothendieck gives an intrinsic description of the 'first floor' of the structure.
(i) Fix an extension 0 → Ω → L → O_X → 0 with Ω invertible.
(ii) Fix a first-order differential operator c_Ω : Ω → L⊗ω, subject to two conditions.
  (a) The composite Ω → L⊗ω → O_X⊗ω = ω is O-linear and an isomorphism. This normalised isomorphism (with a factor -2) is used from now on to identify Ω ≅ ω.
  (b) Leibniz rule: c_Ω(fω) - f c_Ω(ω) = ω⊗df. So for fixed ω the defect is O-linear in f, a map Ω → Ω⊗ω.
Such a pair (L, c_Ω) is claimed to be determined up to unique isomorphism. It is essentially the universal operator d^1 : Ω → P^1(Ω), suitably twisted.

Next step: form the rank-3 bundle V. By the next page, V is filtered with graded pieces Ω, Ω^0, Ω^{-1} where Ω ≅ ω, as for Sym^2 of a rank-2 bundle. P is the associated P^1-bundle (conic) with a section σ. Consider the connections on V that prolong c_Ω. They form the sections of a torsor under Ω⊗ω ≅ ω^{⊗2}, the quadratic differentials. The machine reading 'Ω^2⊗ω' is presumably a slip for Ω⊗ω.

In modern terms this is the algebraic theory of PGL_2-opers, i.e. projective structures or Gunning's 'indigenous bundles', over an arbitrary base S on which 2 is invertible:
- a P^1-bundle P with a connection and a section σ;
- a Kodaira–Spencer-type nondegeneracy condition (a) identifying the normal data with ω;
- the space of such structures being a torsor under H^0(ω^{⊗2}).

The boxed margin note says that giving c_Ω amounts to an isomorphism between the second-order infinitesimal neighbourhoods of σ(X) in P and of the diagonal X in X×_S X. The main text plans to relate the triple (P, σ, c) to formulas of the type O_{P̂} ≅ P^∞_Δ: the formal completion of P along σ is identified with the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal, i.e. the 'osculating/developing map' description of a projective structure, for X/S differentially smooth.

The next page (1.5) uses this to identify sections of P − σ(X), i.e. splittings of P^1(ω), with admissible connections having a horizontal section disjoint from σ.

Context of the dossier (Gauss–Manin, Picard–Fuchs, Cartier operation): this is the oper underlying the Picard–Fuchs equation of a family of curves (e.g. Sym^2 H^1_dR of elliptic curves with Kodaira–Spencer ω_E^2 ≅ Ω^1), with an eye toward characteristic p (Cartier).
errors: Normalisation factors (-2, -1/2) between Ω and ω are juggled between this and the previous page; consistency cannot be checked from the image, but they are the standard factors appearing for Sym^2 (the 'i' of a) is defined via -2).
The torsor group is written as something like Ω^2⊗ω in the transcription; with Ω ≅ ω this would be ω^3. The correct group (and what the previous page says) is Ω⊗ω ≅ ω^{⊗2}.
Uniqueness 'à isomorphisme unique près' of (L, c_Ω) is asserted without proof; it is true (L ≅ twisted P^1(Ω), c_Ω = universal d^1), up to the chosen normalisation.

ideas.what: Characterising the extension L of O_X by an invertible Ω together with a first-order operator Ω → L⊗ω satisfying Leibniz and a symbol-isomorphism condition, as being (up to unique iso) the principal parts P^1(Ω)⊗ω^{-1} with the universal d^1.
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of principal parts / jet bundles; Atiyah-type extension
ideas.where_published: EGA IV 16.3–16.7 (principal parts and differential operators)

ideas.what: Connections on a filtered rank-3 bundle (or P^1-bundle with section σ) prolonging c_Ω, with a nondegenerate Kodaira–Spencer map, form a torsor under ω^{⊗2}; the algebraic, relative theory over S with 2 invertible.
ideas.modern_name: PGL_2-opers / indigenous bundles / projective structures; torsor under quadratic differentials
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1966-67, analytic); Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers, 1990s); Mochizuki (indigenous bundles over arbitrary bases, p odd, 1996-99)

ideas.what: A projective connection/oper structure, i.e. the datum c_Ω, is equivalent to an isomorphism of infinitesimal neighbourhoods of σ(X) in P with those of the diagonal in X×_S X (order 2, and formally O_{P̂} ≅ P^∞_Δ).
ideas.modern_name: Osculating / developing map of a projective structure; formal-neighbourhood description of opers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Gunning, Deligne in analytic setting); Beilinson–Drinfeld, Mochizuki in algebraic setting

ideas.what: Questioning whether invertibility of 2 is really necessary for the theory.
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (later works on dormant opers, e.g. Wakabayashi, treat small characteristic)

missed.claim: Around 1972 Grothendieck writes an algebraic, relative (over arbitrary S, 2 invertible) definition of PGL_2-opers / indigenous bundles. It consists of a filtered bundle with a connection prolonging a universal first-order operator, with a symbol-isomorphism condition. He also shows the space of such connections is a torsor under ω^{⊗2}. This anticipates the algebraic frameworks of Beilinson–Drinfeld and Mochizuki, in a dossier also concerned with the Cartier operation (i.e. a char-p setting).
missed.quote: Elles forment les sections d'un torseur sous ... ≃ ω^{⊗2}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: an early algebraic, base-general treatment of opers in a context tied to Picard–Fuchs and Cartier/p-curvature, close in spirit to Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory and dormant opers.

missed.claim: A planned link between the triple (P, σ, c) and identifications of the formal completion of P along σ with the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal (O_{P̂} ≅ P^∞_Δ), i.e. a jet-theoretic/formal-geometric characterisation of opers over a general base. The question 'is 2 invertible really necessary?' is left open.
missed.quote: Faire le lien avec la filtration (P,σ,c) et les divers formules O_{P̂} ≅ P^∞_Δ (si X/S diff^t lisse)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A formal-neighbourhood characterisation valid without inverting 2 (or in char p via divided-power neighbourhoods) bears on opers in small characteristic and crystalline versions of projective structures.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics (projective structures as a torsor under quadratic differentials, the formal-neighbourhood/osculation description) is classical in the analytic setting and later standard via opers. But a relative algebraic formulation over arbitrary S, written c. 1972 in a Gauss–Manin/Cartier dossier, anticipates Mochizuki-style indigenous bundles and is not in Grothendieck's published texts.
transcription_corrections: 'Ω^2⊗ω' near the end of the main text is likely 'Ω⊗ω' (consistent with the previous page and the ≃ ω^{⊗2}).
'Dire que la suite [?] se donne' – likely 'Donc on peut se donner d'abord l'extension' or similar; uncertain.
'qu'on notera −2i' – the iso Ω ≅ ω is normalised with the factor −2 from the previous page's diagram (*).
'O_{\hat P} ≅ P^∞_Δ' : the image reads roughly 'O_{P̂}^{cpl} ≃ P^∞_{Δ}', the completion of P along σ vs the principal parts of infinite order.
